story.title: U.N. Experts Find Grounds to Believe U.S. Committed War Crimes in Iran Strikes
story.summary: A United Nations fact-finding mission has concluded there are reasonable grounds to believe that the United States committed war crimes during two military strikes in Iran in February. These strikes targeted a school and a sports facility, resulting in significant civilian casualties, including the deaths of 156 civilians, among them 120 children. The findings suggest that these actions may constitute violations of international law.

timeline_highlights.title: Brother of NYPD Officer Who Died from 9/11-Related Cancer Advocates for Victims
timeline_highlights.summary: As the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks approaches, Phil Alvarez, a retired NYPD detective, reflects on his brother Luis's death from cancer linked to toxins at Ground Zero. Alvarez is working to extend the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund to assist others affected by similar health issues. This year, a seventh moment of silence will be observed to honor those who have died from illnesses related to the toxic dust from the attacks.
key_facts: Phil Alvarez's brother, Luis, died from cancer linked to 9/11 toxins.
Alvarez is advocating for the extension of the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund.

timeline_highlights.title: US House Votes Again to End Ongoing Iran Conflict
timeline_highlights.summary: The US House of Representatives has voted for the third time to end the war in Iran by approving a war powers resolution. This resolution aims to prevent the President from continuing military actions without congressional approval. The measure now awaits consideration in the Senate, following more than six months of conflict that was initially expected to be brief.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

related_stories.title: Mbappé Addresses Controversy Over Ceuta Solidarity T-Shirt
related_stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé explained his decision to partially roll up a t-shirt supporting Ceuta residents, stating it was meant to express solidarity with migrants who have lost their lives and those facing difficult conditions. His action has drawn criticism from far-right politicians in Spain and France, who interpreted it as a rejection of Ceuta and its residents.

related_stories.title: Ireland to Boycott Eurovision Again Over Israel's Participation Amid Gaza Conflict
related_stories.summary: Ireland's national broadcaster has announced a boycott of the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest for the second consecutive year. The decision is in protest against Israel's participation, citing the ongoing loss of lives in Gaza as a significant factor. Ireland joins other countries, including the Netherlands, Iceland, Slovenia, and Spain, in this protest.
